Remark
[Bianchi identities and the curvature tensor in normal coordinates]

Source: petersen:page-0244, petersen:page-0245 ↗ lem:pet-ch5-normal-coords-first-order 1. ch5:5.9.42In exponential normal coordinates at $p$, all computed at $p$: (1) taking three derivatives of $x^i=\sum _sg_{is}x^s$ (as in subsection 5.3), show $\partial _i\partial _kg_{jl}+\partial _j\partial _ig_{kl}+\partial _k\partial _jg_{il}=0$; (2) using all four cyclic versions, show $\partial _i\partial _jg_{kl}=\partial _k\partial _lg_{ij}$; (3) using the curvature tensor formula in normal coordinates, show $R_{ikjl}=\partial _i\partial _lg_{kj}-\partial _i\partial _jg_{kl}$; (4) combine (1) and (3) to get $\partial _i\partial _jg_{kl}=\tfrac 13(R_{ikjl}+R_{jkil})$.
